Tier 2: Add a learned long-term preference branch to the existing SASRec model. The current model predicts exclusively from its final sequence representation; explicitly preserving preferences across the history may recover complementary signals. This is motivated by Electronics remaining at HR@10=0.41 versus the baseline’s 0.42, although the results alone do not establish the cause of the plateau.

Focus on model_design and training_evaluation. Compute a padding-masked mean of the existing item embeddings across each observed prefix, then project it into the sequence representation space. Add a learned, feature-wise gate that combines this pooled preference representation with the corresponding SASRec hidden state before candidate scoring. During training, compute pooling causally at every position so future items and prediction targets cannot enter the preference branch. Keep the existing sampled-softmax objective, sampling, optimizer, and hyperparameters unchanged to isolate this architectural change.

Train separate models for all four categories using training seed 42 and the existing input splits, with DATA_DIR remaining os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Select checkpoints using validation HR@10 under the fixed 200-user, 99-unique-negative, seed-42 protocol, and compare the four-category macro-average against 0.5137. Update the predictor writer and saved architecture metadata so working/predict.py reconstructs the gated model and applies identical history processing and learned scoring during host evaluation. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory and leave test inference to the host without accessing hidden test files.
